title: pvVisItM3DC1Reader
body:
## pvVisItM3DC1Reader

Reads HDF5 output of M3D-C1, the high-order finite-element extended-MHD code for tokamak plasmas: the element mesh and the equilibrium mesh become unstructured blocks with node- and cell-centred fields over several time slices. The plugin's VisIt read options stay at their defaults. ParaView 5.13.3 has no native M3D-C1 reader. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Equilibrium and perturbed quantities live on different meshes; select the mesh that carries each array.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- The VisIt plugin's own read options stay at their defaults; the ParaView proxy exposes no property to change them.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItM3DC1Reader`. Identity: `sources/VisItM3DC1Reader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from M3D-C1 data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The M3D-C1 plugin offers the node- and cell-centred fields of the M3D-C1 output (field components, equilibrium quantities); which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single M3D-C1 file to read (.h5); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The M3D-C1 plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the M3D-C1 meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The M3D-C1 plugin reports meshes such as "mesh" and "equilibrium/mesh" built from the code's triangular elements. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from M3D-C1 data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The M3D-C1 plugin offers the node- and cell-centred fields of the M3D-C1 output (field components, equilibrium quantities); which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItM3DC1Reader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
